description: We are a team of two passionate about space, aerospace engineering, and software development. We are particularly interested in exploring how technology and engineering make space exploration possible. We enjoy building software-driven projects, researching new technologies, and turning complex ideas into engaging experiences.
summary: Marswalk is an interactive Mars exploration simulator that helps people explore how terrain and mission goals can shape a human EVA route. Users begin on a 3D Mars globe, choose a start and destination, set a crew size, and identify regions of scientific interest. They then enter a first-person simulation in Jezero Crater, where a route is planned over HiRISE terrain data using slope, roughness, and data availability. Users can compare route preferences, follow a visible guide, or activate automatic travel. A minimap offers terrain and imagery views alongside clearly labeled scenario-based environmental views. Marswalk combines real planetary datasets with an accessible, immersive experience to make route-planning trade-offs easier to understand. It is an educational planning demonstration, not an operational safety assessment.
details:
Marswalk turns Mars terrain data into an interactive journey. On the opening screen, users explore a 3D Mars globe, choose a start and destination, set a crew size, and select types of regions that may matter to a scientific mission. The globe provides mission context. The playable first-person area is a local HiRISE terrain patch in Jezero Crater; selections outside that area use the Jezero demonstration route.

Within the simulation, an A* planner compares possible paths using local terrain slope, roughness, and valid elevation data. Users can choose balanced, shorter, or gentler route preferences. A visible route guide, minimap, manual movement, Mars-gravity-inspired jumping, and automatic travel make the result easy to explore. The minimap includes imagery and topographic views. Thermal, atmospheric, and radiation views are labeled scenario models rather than direct measurements.

We built the application with JavaScript ES modules, WebGL2, Canvas 2D, and a browser-based route-planning worker. Its planetary context and Jezero scene use NASA mission resources and HiRISE data, with USGS mapping resources identified separately below. The creative focus is to let users experience how different route priorities change an EVA journey while keeping the source and limits of each data layer visible.

Marswalk is intended for education and exploration. Its route score is a terrain-based walkability indicator under chosen scenario settings. It does not certify a route as safe, reproduce a real human Mars mission, or provide live mission telemetry.
